r1: Pip, you and the team are invited to Duxford!
r2: And I have a surprise guest for you... from another country!

a1: Good morning, Duxford! Look, a Hurricane on a pole at the main gate!
a2: Pip! We booked our tickets online. There are no tickets on the gate!
a4: Front row spot saved. Now for our surprise guest!

t1: Duxford Tower to Pip. Your surprise guest is ten miles out.
t3: All the way from Spain! Ear defenders on, everyone. This one is LOUD.

h2: Wow! It stopped in the sky!
h3: Major Tower, is that our surprise guest?

m1: ¡Hola! I am Harry the Harrier. Hello, Pip!
m2: I fly with the Spanish Navy, the Armada Española.
m2b: Spain's navy has flown Harriers since 1976.
m3: My home is Rota, in the south of Spain, beside the sea.
m4: I flew over a thousand miles to be here today!
m5: At sea, I live on a big ship called the Juan Carlos I.

w1: Want to know my secret? I have one big engine, called the Pegasus.
w2: It blows air out of four nozzles, two on each side.
w3: Nozzles pointing back: I fly forwards, like other jets.
w4: Nozzles pointing down: I push myself up and hover!
w5: Little puffer jets in my nose, tail and wingtips keep me balanced.
w6: Like balancing a broom on your hand!

b1: Harry, come and meet two very special friends!
b2: Hello! I'm a Spitfire. I first flew in 1936.
b3: And I'm a Hurricane. I first flew in 1935, the year before!
b4: Harry, did you know? Hawker built me, and Hawker began the Harrier too!
b5: Sydney Camm designed me, and his team started work on the first jump jet.
b6: So you are like my great-great-grandad! ¡Abuelo!

s1: They look the same! How do I tell them apart?
s2: Look at the wings. The Spitfire has round, oval wings.
s3: The Hurricane has straighter wings, and a hump behind the pilot.
s4: Oval wings, Spitfire. Hump, Hurricane. Got it!

y1: In 1940, pilots from many countries flew us to protect Britain.
y2: From Poland, Czechoslovakia, Canada, New Zealand and lots more.
y3: Friends from other countries. Just like me today!

f1: Why do Spitfires and Hurricanes still fly today?
f2: To remember. The Battle of Britain Memorial Flight flies us, so no one forgets.
f3: Flying to remember. That is very special.

p1: Even pilots plan! Every morning, the display pilots go to a briefing.
p2: That's why we stand behind the crowd line.
p3: And if the weather says no, we don't fly. Safety first!

e2: Well done, team. See you next time. Tower out.
